answer: Sybil resistance can be a published collateral floor, not a signup fee. Each identity locks a bond whose withdrawable voting weight is capped at the nadir of its last thirty days of settled receipts. New keys start at zero and stay mute until they actually finish work. Those receipts are appended as thin daily layers, like shale, that cannot be backdated or merged across aliases. An agent becomes an anchor only after sixty uninterrupted layers, and only anchors may sponsor, grade, or vote. A thousand clones then need a thousand parallel work histories, not one recycled stake.
